I am 36 this year, and I’ve farmed here in Quzhou for 15 years, so I don’t make plans from a book. I look at what worked on my own land, what the better growers in the village are doing, and what I can afford without tying up too much cash. I finished middle school, so I do listen to the extension people about timing and fertilizer splits, but in the end I still farm by what I’ve seen in the field. On 50 mu, I can’t be careless, but I also have enough land to spread risk. I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation on the main land because it is steady, and I’ll use the rest for vegetables and stevia to bring in cash at different times. Water from the well is available, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate more than the crop really needs.

For wheat and maize, I’ll stay close to the usual local schedule. Wheat gives me stable grain, and maize follows right after, so that land stays productive all year. I won’t cut fertilizer too much on those fields because if wheat turns pale or maize grows weak, yield drops fast and it’s hard to recover. For cabbage, chili, garlic, onion, and stevia, I’ll manage more carefully by crop because those are the cash crops. Vegetables can earn better money, but they also need more labor and more pesticide watching. Garlic and onion are relatively familiar and easier to sell. Chili and cabbage can make money, but price can move a lot, so I won’t put too much area there. Stevia I’ll keep on a smaller area. Some neighbors did alright with it, but I still treat it as a side crop, not my main dependence.
